solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Awful trauma, with one adult displaced by international court

indicators.note: something awful is a mess, so the letters of trauma are jumbled
one thing displaced by another is swapped out for it, so one letter is replaced

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for adult, here a single one of the two in trauma

explanation.surface: A dreadful shock suffered by a grown-up at the international court in The Hague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'International court' looks like one phrase, but only 'international' gives I; 'court' is the definition. Swapping an A for I gives TRIUMA, which 'Awful' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrium is an open central courtyard or hall in a building, so a court in the architectural sense.

clue.text: Banter, as such, going over head of inmate, fellow prisoner

indicators.note: a thing going over others covers them, so the outer piece wraps round the rest

parts.note: per se is Latin for as such, in itself

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: lag is British slang for a convict, as in old lag

explanation.surface: Joking talk passing between one inmate and a fellow prisoner in a cell.
explanation.walkthrough: Latin PER SE wraps I, F and LAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Persiflage is light, mocking banter or frivolous teasing talk, so a direct synonym.

clue.text: Take orders from old boy you once sent up

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word sent up is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: ye is the archaic form of you

explanation.surface: A former pupil is told to do as he is told, having once mocked you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent up' looks like mockery but in a down clue it reverses YE to EY.
explanation.definitionFit: To obey someone is to carry out their instructions, the plain meaning of following orders.

clue.text: A reportedly depressed woman in plant

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word heard rather than seen, so the sound of a word is used

parts.note: depressed means low in spirits
Vera is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman feeling down, said to be among the greenery.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloe vera is a succulent plant whose sap is used in soothing gels and cosmetics.

clue.text: Against the current new look of tempuras

indicators.note: giving a new look to the letters of tempuras means rearranging them

explanation.surface: A food stylist gives tempura dishes a fresh appearance, bucking the trend.
explanation.definitionFit: Going upstream is travelling against the flow of a river, opposite to the current.

clue.text: Colour of English silver received by groom

indicators.note: something received by another is taken in, so it goes inside

parts.note: to groom oneself is to preen, tidy one's appearance
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A bridegroom is given English silverware whose shade is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' looks like a bridegroom, but it is the verb, giving PREEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Pea green is a pale yellowish-green shade named after the vegetable.

clue.text: Took longer than was necessary? Perhaps chef did, with what he was given

definitions.meaning: to make a meal of something is an idiom for spending more effort or time on a task than needed

definitions.text: Perhaps chef did, with what he was given
definitions.meaning: literally, a cook turns the ingredients handed to him into a dish

explanation.surface: A slow worker's dawdling is compared to a cook preparing supplied food.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means overdoing a task, and taken literally describes a cook producing food from ingredients.

clue.text: Wholly entertained by wicked song

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is held within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: wicked means bad
wholly means all, entirely

explanation.surface: A wicked person is completely amused by a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a song, typically narrative or sentimental, so the definition gives its category.

clue.text: A boundary that's upset alliance

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns a word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: in cricket a six is a boundary hit clearing the rope on the full

explanation.surface: A border dispute that disrupted a pact between nations.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a SIX is a hit over the boundary rope; 'upset' reverses it to XIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Axis was the wartime alliance of Germany, Italy and Japan, so a coalition of powers.

clue.text: Is concerned about one getting tooth decay

indicators.note: about here means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to care is to be concerned
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone worries about a person with a rotting tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: Caries is the medical term for decay of teeth or bone, the cause of cavities.

clue.text: US lawyer wisely involved Irish actor

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, a US prosecuting lawyer

indicators.note: involved means intricate, tangled, so the letters of wisely are mixed up

explanation.surface: An American attorney sensibly took part in a case concerning an actor from Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Day-Lewis is an Irish-British actor, three-time Oscar winner for Best Actor.

clue.text: I'm career chef, originally a product of France

indicators.note: originally here suggests an original or inventive arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A professional cook boasts about a French product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' looks like it picks first letters, but it signals an anagram of all twelve.
explanation.definitionFit: Crème fraîche is a thick soured cream made in France, a French dairy product.

clue.text: Arrest by copper with appeal of reduced charge

parts.note: to arrest a suspect is to catch them
a penny is a copper coin; coppers is British slang for small change

explanation.surface: A police officer makes an arrest, and the suspect appeals to have the charge lowered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Catchpenny describes cheap goods made to attract buyers by low price rather than quality.

clue.text: Video not working, love?

indicators.note: working means operating or being reworked, so the letters are rearranged; with not, the surface reads broken

explanation.surface: Someone asks a partner if the video recorder has broken down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not working' reads as one phrase, but 'not' is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Devotion is deep love or loyal affection, so love is an example; hence the question mark.

clue.text: Drove that woman daft, initially

parts.note: her refers to a woman already mentioned

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone drove a woman crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drove' looks like a verb but is a noun, a flock of animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A drove is a group of animals driven together, synonymous with a moving flock of cattle.

clue.text: Find out about record surplus

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
over means left over, in excess

explanation.surface: Someone learns of an excess of records in a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover something is to learn of it or come upon it, finding out about it.

clue.text: First of riders in a lease causes alarm

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a let is a lease, as when property is let

indicators.note: first of means take the initial letter

explanation.surface: A clause about the first horse riders in a rental agreement causes worry.
explanation.definitionFit: An alert is a warning signal, so the same as an alarm.

clue.text: Top copy plus ten

parts.note: to ape is to copy or imitate
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A photocopy of the best ten.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the highest point or peak of something, the top.

clue.text: Second, athletes who surprisingly get everyone's praise in event

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests an unexpected arrangement, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Runners-up at an athletics meet unexpectedly win all the acclaim.
explanation.definitionFit: To steal the show is an idiom for outshining everyone else and winning the applause at an event.

clue.text: Greek character, across sole of foot, finds scar

indicators.note: across means lying over, so the Greek letter spans the other piece

parts.note: sigma is the eighteenth letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: the sole is the bottom, in a down clue the last letter

explanation.surface: A Greek man with a mark on the bottom of his foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole of foot' sounds anatomical but gives T, its bottom letter in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of disgrace, figuratively a scar or brand left on someone.

clue.text: Leader of clog dance gets cut

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: The head of a clog-dancing troupe is injured.
explanation.definitionFit: To chop is to cut with a sharp blow, as with an axe.

clue.text: Film cancelled — hurry away

parts.note: to film a scene is to shoot it
a cancelled event is off

explanation.surface: Movie production called off, so the crew rushes home.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoot off is an informal phrasal verb for leaving quickly, dashing away.

clue.text: Price offered not even by head of Smithsonian

parts.note: odd numbers are not even

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A bid that is uneven made by the director of the museum.
explanation.walkthrough: The Smithsonian is a museum in Washington; only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: The odds are the price offered by a bookmaker on a bet, as in betting.

clue.text: Priest's team getting recipe for magic potion

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Bible who raised Samuel
XI is eleven, a cricket or football team
R is an abbreviation for recipe, from Latin recipe, take

explanation.surface: A priest's side receives instructions for a magical drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An elixir is a magical potion supposed to prolong life or turn base metal into gold.

clue.text: 23 looked at in broadcast

parts.note: the answer to 23 down, a bookmaker's price; SP is starting price
read means looked at, past tense

explanation.surface: The betting prices were scanned on a radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 refers to the answer at 23 down; SP means starting price, the odds at a race's start.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread news or seed is to broadcast it, scatter widely.

clue.text: Guys in principle responsible for block of apartments

indicators.note: in shows one piece placed inside another

parts.note: a tenet is a principle or belief
guys means men

explanation.surface: The men in charge of an apartment building, in principle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a large building divided into flats, especially in Scotland or older cities.
